script: In 1942, a Spanish chicken farmer walked into British intelligence with an insane offer. His name was Juan Pujol, and he wanted to spy against the Nazis, for free. Britain turned him down. So he built an entire fake spy network from scratch, inventing twenty-seven agents who never existed, and sold his fake reports straight to German intelligence. The Nazis loved him so much they gave him a medal. Only then did the British recruit him for real, codename Garbo. When D-Day came, his fictional agents convinced Hitler the real invasion was still coming later, at Calais. Hitler held back his best tank divisions for weeks. One farmer's imaginary spy ring helped win the war.
